translation: Target is the proposition stating that for every set K of arithmetic sentences (in the language ℒₒᵣ) and every arithmetic theory F, assuming F is recursively enumerable and every theorem of 𝗜𝚺₁ is a theorem of F, if K (viewed as an arithmetic theory) is consistent (does not prove a contradiction), then it is not the case that both (1) K equals the set of all first-order theorems of F ({σ | F ⊢ σ}) and (2) the consistency sentence of F.craig—that is, ¬Prov_{F.craig}(⌜⊥⌝), where F.craig is the Δ₁-presented axiom set with the same theorems as F given by Craig's trick and Prov_{F.craig} is the standard provability predicate built from that Δ₁ presentation—belongs to K. Note that consistency is assumed directly on K (not on F separately), F is required only to be recursively enumerable rather than Δ₁-presented, and no truth or soundness assumption is made on K or F.

divergences.description: Consistency replaces soundness in the hypothesis of [P-C1]: Chalmers assumes the formal system F is sound, whereas Target only assumes K is consistent (Def4 K, equivalent under K = F.theory to consistency of F). This is a harmless strengthening of the theorem.

Relative to [P-K359], Target formalizes the impossibility of counting F's consistency among K's conclusions (matching [P-C1]) rather than knowing that F_e 'works correctly' (soundness, F_e ⊆ T, which plain arithmetic cannot express as a single sentence), and drops the epistemic disjunct ¬K(K = F_e) ('we do not know the exact specification of the computer'), which cannot be expressed without an object-language knowledge operator; given K = F.theory, ruling out Con(F) ∈ K is logically stronger than the disjunction in [P-K359].

Epistemic attitude ('see that' in [P-C1], 'know' in [P-K359]) is approximated by plain set membership (∈ K) in the metalanguage, since first-order arithmetic has no knowledge operator (as declared separately by the author).

Target models a formal system or theorem-proving computer extensionally as a recursively enumerable set of arithmetic sentences F and defines 'F's consistency' via a single noncomputably chosen Craig-trick Δ₁ presentation (F.craig.consistent.val), rather than quantifying over arbitrary Δ₁ presentations or tying the consistency sentence to a specific machine specification F_e (abstracting away the intensionality of consistency sentences).

Target restricts 'reasoning powers' / 'mathematical intuition' and formal systems to first-order arithmetic (ℒₒᵣ) and adds the explicit arithmetical strength hypothesis 𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F, which the source passages leave implicit in invoking Gödel's incompleteness results.

judgement.summary: Target faithfully captures the claimed impossibility—a consistent set of arithmetic sentences cannot both equal the theorems of a sufficiently strong RE theory F and contain F's consistency sentence—matching [P-C1] closely and strengthening the relevant consequence of [P-K359]. Its divergences are minor formalization choices and declared limitations of plain arithmetic: restricting to ℒₒᵣ with 𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F, using consistency instead of soundness, using a Craig-trick presentation for Con(F), and replacing epistemic operators with set membership.
